the sustainable production of a high value-added compound, butyl levuliate, from a biomass-derived platform, furfuryl alcohols, was achieved adopting an easily recyclable commercial catalyst, Aquivion\({}^{\text{\text{\tiny\textregistered}}}\) P87S.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Aquivion(r), as a recyclable and robust heterogeneous catalyst for the production of BL from FA is a promising alternative to the use of corrosives and harmful mineral acids.
the use of Aquivion(r)-P87S resin is a sustainable approach to the production of butyl esters from biomass derived platform chemicals, such as FA.

a sustainable process to produce BL from FA is achieved, using a commercial perfluorinated resin as a heterogeneous catalyst, in a one-step reaction in butanol, without the use of corrosives, heavy metals, and in a solvent free system.
